headline: The finder's transcription work is accurate: I re-read five programs from page images at random (Tic-Tac-Toe 72 lines, Traffic Light 22 lines, Traffic Light w/ Pedestrian Control 26 lines, Relay AND 10 lines, basic sequence recognition 38 lines, Book I Exp 12+13 15 lines) and found ZERO transcription errors and zero hallucinated lines. The refutations are therefore not about accuracy - they are about (a) a whole primary source the finder never opened, (b) ~13 programs it never transcribed, (c) one 'anomaly' it invented, and (d) several 'not settled by the sources' items that ARE settled.

refuted.claim: find-programs.json D2 / VI-TICTACTOE per_line_flags: the printed line '4G/5N' in the Tic-Tac-Toe table is anomalous; '4N/5N' would be the ordered reading and is the plausible intended line.
refuted.correction: REFUTED. '4G/5N' is correct as printed and is not a typographic error. It is the middle member of a three-link chain that the same table prints in full: 3G/4N (col 2), 4G/5N (col 3), 5G/6N (col 4). The finder noticed 4G/5N sits out of alphabetical order after 4L/M6t but did not notice that 5G/6N sits out of order in EXACTLY the same relative slot in column 4 (immediately after 5L/M4t). Two identical out-of-order placements in consecutive columns is a printing pattern, not a typo. The finder's proposed '4N/5N' would break the relay-G-to-relay-N chain and is wrong; the simulator must wire 4G/5N. The finder also missed the parallel that 3G, 4G and 5G each appear twice in the table (3G/D7 + 3G/4N, 4G/D5 + 4G/5N, 5G/D3 + 5G/6N), so '4G appears twice' is not evidence of an error either.
refuted.evidence: book5-6.pdf PDF page 62 (printed p56), read at 110 dpi. Column 2 rows 7-8: '3G/D7', '3G/4N'. Column 3 rows 3 and 9: '4G/D5', '4G/5N'. Column 4 rows 2 and 6: '5G/6N', '6G/D1'. [verified]
refuted.severity: high - the finder's flag would tempt an implementer to 'fix' a correct line

refuted.claim: not_settled_by_the_sources: 'Whether the six section minus terminals (1- .. 6-) and plus terminals are one common supply rail or six separately-fused nodes. ... no page says so.' And headline_findings: 'M+ and M- ... Whether they are physically part of the MATRIX block or a separate motor-power pair is NOT settled by the manuals.'
refuted.correction: REFUTED - both are settled, in print, by a primary source the finder never opened. The errata sheet states flatly: 'All + and - terminals are connected together. For example, a connection to 1+ is the same as a connection to 3+, 6+, or M+. Similarly, a connection to 2- is the same as a connection to 4-, 5-, or M-.' So every section plus terminal and M+ are one node; every section minus terminal and M- are one node. This also disposes of the finder's discrepancy D3 (Book I Exp 12 '6-/D18' vs Exp 13 '5-/D18'): both are the same node, no typo exists.
refuted.evidence: errata.pdf, page 1, left column, second paragraph. [verified]
refuted.severity: high - this is a first-order simulator netlist fact

refuted.claim: D7 / not_settled: how many COMMON terminals there physically are is 'NOT settled by the manuals; must be settled from the panel photograph.'
refuted.correction: DOWNGRADED to essentially settled. The errata sheet enumerates common-terminal sets by hole count: 'common terminals are any set of terminals which are interconnected: for instance, the two terminals at 6R, the six at M10, or the four at 3com.' So '3com' is one terminal with FOUR interconnected holes, and there is a com terminal per section (1com..6com). That makes Book I's 'The four COMMON terminals are connected together' a count of the four holes of one COMMON terminal, exactly as the preceding sentence in Book I ('The terminals with four holes labeled COMMON') already implies. Book I is not contradicting Books III-VI; the finder read an ambiguity into it. I re-read the Book I sentence and it is quoted accurately by the finder - the quote is fine, the 'unresolvable' conclusion is not.
refuted.evidence: errata.pdf page 1, left column, third paragraph. book1.txt lines 1310-1322 (printed p25, AUXILIARY TERMINALS). [verified for the errata text; the inference that 'four' = holes is [likely]]

refuted.claim: transcription_policy.tag_meaning defines [verified] as 'read by me in a rendered page image ... OR unambiguous body prose in a clean OCR layer that I cross-checked against a second printing of the same program.'
refuted.correction: REFUTED as a policy deviation. The project rule is [verified] = read in a primary source page image or the panel photograph. The finder's second clause admits OCR-only claims to [verified] on the strength of self-consistency, which is precisely the failure mode the brief warns about ('The OCR is good on body text and unreliable on display headings, tables, and figure callouts' - and every program listing IS a display block, not body text). In practice the finder's OCR reads survived my spot checks, so this did not produce a wrong claim in my sample; but the tag on any program marked verified without an image read should be read as [likely].
refuted.evidence: find-programs.json lines 38-42 vs the project brief's rule 2. [verified]
refuted.severity: medium - hygiene, affects how downstream agents should trust the 'verified' count of 32

refuted.claim: D4: Book V Exp 4 vs Exp 5 rotary/motor connections are a 'discrepancy'; 'Exp 4 puts TWO rotary terminals on M-.'
refuted.correction: DOWNGRADED - not a discrepancy. Both printings are image-confirmed by me and both are electrically sensible. Exp 4: D16/M- (wiper to minus), D17/M-, D18/M+ (motor across the rail, one polarity). Exp 5: D16/M-, D17/M+ (motor the other polarity) with D18 taken over by the pedestrian interrupt (5J/D18). Given R4 (all + are one node, all - are one node) there is nothing anomalous about two rotary terminals landing on M-. Record it as a polarity/wiring difference between two programs, not as a printing discrepancy needing resolution.
refuted.evidence: book5-6.pdf PDF page 11 (printed p5) @130 dpi, both program blocks read in full. [verified]

upgraded.was: VI-SEQREC / D1: the Combination Lock printing reads 5A/6J while Secret Code and Electronic Maze read 6A/6J; 'Both are primary. Recorded, not resolved.'
upgraded.now: The observation is CONFIRMED - I independently image-read book5-6.pdf PDF page 58 (printed p52) at 130 dpi and the Combination Lock printing does read '5A/6J', in column 4 row 3, in a 38-line block otherwise identical to the finder's list. But the finder should have resolved it, and it is resolvable from the same page: the 38-line circuit contains '6B/6-' and contains NO 5B connection at all. A light needs both its A and its B terminal wired, so '5A/6J' would leave light 5 with no return path AND leave light 6 (whose 6B/6- IS wired) undriven - while the same page's prose says 'light 6 comes on when an error is made'. 6A/6J is therefore the correct reading and the Combination Lock printing carries a 6->5 typo. Tag the conclusion [likely] (electrical inference from image-verified text), not [verified].

That is direct primary evidence that relay pull-in is marginal and voltage-dependent in the real machine - a modelling fact the finder did not have.

missed.what: The errata sheet - docs/research/raw/pdf/errata.pdf (duplicate at minivac601-errata.pdf) - was never opened. It sits in the same directory as the three book PDFs the finder did read. It is primary: 'Notes and Corrections to the Minivac Manual', Scientific Development Corporation, 372 Main Street, Watertown, Massachusetts, issued 'In response to questions from MINIVAC owners.' It contains program-level corrections to EIGHT programs the finder transcribed, one complete additional program, two complete circuit-modification sets, and several global electrical facts.
missed.detail: See errata_program_corrections and errata_global_facts below for the full transcription.

missed.what: Every program in Book II. The finder's 84-program list contains exactly one Book II entry, and that entry (II-3STMT) is actually Book III (see R3). Book II - 'What is a Digital Computer?' - contains at least eleven wiring programs, listed with full transcriptions below in missed_programs_book_ii. Two of them are directly corrected by the errata sheet, which is how I found the gap.
missed.detail: Experiments 1-7 plus four memory-circuit programs, printed pp.6-15.

missed.what: Two Book III programs: 'The Operation EITHER BUT NOT BOTH' (printed p41, pushbutton XOR, 5 connections) and 'The Relay EITHER BUT NOT BOTH Circuit' (printed p44, 11 connections). The Book III CONTENTS page lists 'The Relay EITHER BUT NOT BOTH circuit ... 44' between the Relay NOT circuit (which the finder DID transcribe as III-RELAYNOT) and the next section, so it was skipped inside a range the finder was already reading.

The errata's alternate THREE-BIT BINARY COUNTER program (48 connections, 4 columns x 12 rows) - a complete program that appears in no book. The errata says the Book IV counter 'strains' the relays and that this alternate 'by-passes the relay indicator lights so that full voltage is supplied to the relay coils'. Any conformance suite that runs IV-EXP1 needs this one too.

The errata's Book V pages 21-22 note: 'when programming a geometric form or a numeral for recognition, be sure that the connections from M10 are made to the TOP terminals in the matrix.' The finder's headline finding about V-EXP12 (Arabic Numeral Recognition) mentions 'four wires each on M10 and M11' but not the top-terminal rule, which is exactly the sort of thing a simulator gets wrong.

Two further PDFs sit in raw/pdf that the finder neither read nor listed as out of scope: maintenance-manual.pdf (relay/motor adjustment - bears on the relay timing model) and book7-capacitor-resistor.pdf, whose cover reads 'Minivac 601/6010 Capacitor/Resistor Manual' and which contains rotary-switch program fragments. The latter is a 601/6010 JOINT document and is a live 6010-contamination risk for any later agent; it should be explicitly scoped in or out.

The errata's four game notes for Book VI, which change observable behaviour the finder recorded: Secret Code and Electronic Maze re-set by turning power off then on; Combination Lock re-sets by turning the rotary switch through one complete revolution; Tic-Tac-Toe 'if the game is a tie, MINIVAC will indicate a tie on the fifth move but will not indicate a move into the last available space'; Match Game's 'To Play' text is corrected to 'Turn the rotary switch to 15' (i.e. the dial is set by hand, NOT by pushbutton 3 as the finder's procedure_as_printed step 1 says); Mind Reading Trick - zero is considered even; Reaction Time Tester - add dummy rotary connections or cover the dial.

errata_global_facts.claim: All + and - terminals are connected together. A connection to 1+ is the same as 3+, 6+, or M+. A connection to 2- is the same as 4-, 5-, or M-.

Common terminals are any set of interconnected terminals - 'the two terminals at 6R, the six at M10, or the four at 3com'. Programs may be routed through unused common terminals to save wire length: 1X/6A == 1X/4R + 4R/6A, or 1X/4com + 4com/6A.
Power must be OFF while wiring or unwiring a program, to prevent accidental short circuits.
A programming error can cause a short circuit; the circuit breaker must be pushed after correcting it.
Some programs are not designed for high-speed operation; carry the procedure out slowly.
Relay arms can be physically obstructed by short programming wires; long wires are recommended so wires do not interfere with relay arm movement.

The rotary switch pointer can stop BETWEEN adjacent terminals (e.g. between D6 and D7) and make proper contact with neither - a real failure mode the simulator may want to model or explicitly exclude.
errata_global_facts.cite: errata.pdf p3, BOOK V page 11 note

errata_global_facts.claim: SDC was preparing a second edition of the Minivac Manual; correspondence to the Editor, Linda G. Sprague.

The errata sheet's own address line, printed at the foot: '372 Main Street, Watertown, Massachusetts'. This is a THIRD primary attestation of the Watertown address (with the Book V-VI and Book II-III-IV copyright pages) and does NOT resolve the standing Watertown-vs-Cambridge panel-legend discrepancy - it only weights the paper side. Do not treat it as resolving it.

programs.name: Experiment 1: Binary Input
programs.read_from: pdftotext -layout OCR of PDF p12; clean typeset block, not image-verified
programs.behaviour: Pushbutton down = 1, up = 0; each section's relay latches the bit and the relay indicator light shows it. Pushbutton 6 clears all six relays. Worked example in the text stores 10011 (19).

programs.name: Experiment 2: Decimal Input
programs.connection_count_note: The OCR block yields 23 distinct lines in a 5x5 grid; two cells appear to be blank in columns 4 and 5. NOT image-verified - the count needs an image read before use. [unverified as to count]
programs.behaviour: Turn the DECIMAL INPUT-OUTPUT knob to a digit 1-5 and push pushbutton 5 to store it; the relay indicator light of that section number comes on. Pushbutton 6 clears. Text notes decimal input is limited to 0-15 in general but this program covers 1-5.

programs.name: Experiment 3: Secondary Storage
programs.read_from: page image, book2-3-4.pdf PDF p15 @150 dpi
programs.behaviour: Slide switch left = 1 (light 1 ON), right = 0 (light 1 OFF). Convention stated on the same page: switch right = 0, switch left = 1.

programs.name: Manual Relay Memory Circuit
programs.behaviour: Relay 1 remembers 1 only while pushbutton 1 is held down; releasing it reverts to 0.

programs.name: Self-Locking Relay Memory Circuit
programs.behaviour: Adds 1C/1A, giving a second current path through the relay's own normally-open contact - the relay latches ON and cannot be cleared except by removing power.

programs.name: Two-Button Relay Memory Circuit (two-input flip-flop)
programs.read_from: page image, book2-3-4.pdf PDF p17 @130 dpi
programs.errata: errata.pdf, BOOK II page 11: change 1A/1C to 1A/1G, and delete the 1A/1C connection on the circuit diagram. Corrected last line = 1A/1G.
programs.behaviour: Pushbutton 1 = 'forget 0, remember 1'; pushbutton 2 (normally-closed contacts, via 2Z) = 'forget 1, remember 0'. Book II names this the two-input flip-flop.

programs.name: The Single Input Flip-Flop (Book II printing)
programs.behaviour: One pushbutton (1) toggles the stored bit. Light 1 ON = remembering 1. NOTE: this is a Book II printing, distinct from the finder's IV-FF1 / IV-FF2 (Book IV, printed pp.69-70). Whether the three printings are the same 14 wires is NOT settled - needs a side-by-side image read.
programs.warning: Do NOT assume this equals the finder's IV-FF1 (16 connections) or IV-FF2 (14 connections). Three separate printings exist.

programs.name: Experiment 4: Control
programs.behaviour: Pushbutton 5 energises relay 5; relay 5's contacts energise relay 6; relay 6 closes the motor RUN circuit. A chain demonstrating that the processing unit controls the machine's own operations.

programs.name: Experiment 5: Decision Making (equality comparator)
programs.behaviour: Pushbuttons 1 and 2 carry the two binary numbers to compare. Relay 3 comes ON if they are equal, goes OFF if not.

programs.name: Experiment 6: Arithmetic (one-bit adder)
programs.errata: errata.pdf, BOOK II page 14: change 2Z/2C to 2X/2C.
programs.behaviour: Pushbuttons 1 and 2 are the addends (up = 0, down = 1). Light 1 ON = answer 1; light 2 ON = answer 2; no lights = 0.

programs.name: Experiment 7: Decimal Output
programs.read_from: OCR of PDF p21; the block is 4 columns and includes a stray '6Z' label above the table that may be part of a diagram, not the program
programs.count_warning: The OCR grid is 4 columns of 5 with one short column; my reconstruction is 16 lines but the layout is ambiguous and the isolated '6Z' is unexplained. NOT image-verified. [unverified as to completeness]
programs.behaviour: Slide switches 1-6 (secondary storage) drive the rotary switch to display the stored number as decimal output. All switches start RIGHT.

missed_programs_book_iii.name: The Operation 'EITHER BUT NOT BOTH' (pushbutton XOR)
missed_programs_book_iii.behaviour: Light 3 = statement C. The program uses the pushbutton contacts so that light 3 comes on if either pushbutton 1 or pushbutton 2 is pushed, but not if both are. errata.pdf notes this operation is 'often referred to as the EXCLUSIVE OR'.

missed_programs_book_iii.name: The Relay EITHER BUT NOT BOTH Circuit
missed_programs_book_iii.behaviour: Relay XOR using the cross-coupled J/G contact pair of the two relays. Completes the Book III set of four relay logic circuits (AND, OR, NOT, EITHER-BUT-NOT-BOTH); the finder transcribed the first three and stopped.

confirmed_unchanged.program: coverage of Books V and VI
confirmed_unchanged.what: Complete. I checked both CONTENTS pages against the finder's program list: all 21 Book V experiments, all four Book V non-experiment circuits (translation, job selection, associative memory, maze solver, flashing lights, super circuit) and all eleven Book VI games are present. 'Mate Selection' (Book V p42) has no separate program - the text says it reuses the Job Selection program with different questionnaires, so its absence is correct.

still_not_settled: The Watertown vs Cambridge address split. Three paper primaries (Book II-III-IV copyright page, Book V-VI copyright page, errata sheet header and footer) all say '372 Main Street, Watertown, Massachusetts'; the panel legend reportedly says Cambridge. I did not open the panel photograph - it is another agent's primary. Still unresolved, and the errata does not resolve it.

The ring order of the nine matrix squares behind Tic-Tac-Toe's 'move 4 / move 5 squares to the right' rule. Nothing in Book VI, Book I or the errata restates the numbering. Needs the panel photograph.
Book II Experiment 2 and Experiment 7 connection counts (23 and 16 by my OCR reconstruction, in grids whose column breaks are ambiguous). Needs one image read each of book2-3-4.pdf PDF p13 and p21.
The errata's Book III page 36 correction body, which is illegible in the OCR layer and was cut off in my image. Needs a targeted read of errata.pdf page 2, right column.
The errata's alternate three-bit binary counter program: transcribed from OCR only, two lines carry OCR damage. Needs errata.pdf page 2 right column at 300+ dpi.
Whether Book II's single-input flip-flop (14 wires) is the same program as Book IV's IV-FF1 (16 wires) and IV-FF2 (14 wires). Three printings, not cross-checked.
Book I answer pages (printed 29-32) - the finder's 20 problem answers remain hand-lettered and [unverified]; the errata adds notes for Problems 7 and 18 but not the wiring.
Rotary-switch dial speed in rpm. Still nowhere in the manuals or the errata.
Whether book7-capacitor-resistor.pdf (a joint '601/6010' document) is in scope, and whether the maintenance manual's relay/motor adjustment data should feed the timing model.
verdict: The finder's transcriptions are trustworthy - I re-read ten programs from page images and found not one wrong or hallucinated line, including the 72-line Tic-Tac-Toe table it claimed as its centrepiece. The file's failures are of scope and of judgement: it never opened errata.pdf, sitting in the same directory, which corrects eight of its own transcribed programs, adds a 48-wire program, and settles three of its 'not settled by the sources' items outright; it transcribed zero of Book II's eleven programs and skipped two Book III circuits; and its one flagged Tic-Tac-Toe 'anomaly' is a false alarm that would corrupt a correct line if acted on.
